title: What the DAAM: Interpreting Stable Diffusion Using Cross Attention
role: Read-out method and the one pooled measurement linking same-category noun pairs to cross-attention overlap and to one object going missing; supports cross-attention overlap as a predictor, offers no fix
enters: cross-attention: the two nouns' summed attention maps overlap more for same-category (WordNet cohyponym) pairs and for failed images
enters_evidence: correlational measurement on 1,000 'a(n) X and a(n) Y' prompts: DAAM map mIoU 46.7 cohyponym vs 22.9 non-cohyponym; overlap read from the same image whose failure is scored, summed over all 30 steps, so cause is argued, not tested
changes: nothing; DAAM sums bicubically upscaled cross-attention maps over heads, all layers (16, 32, 64 resolution) and all 30 steps, then thresholds at 0.4 of the max; adjective probe fixes attention maps to a seed prompt (Prompt-to-Prompt)
training: nothing trained; needs only the prompt and the word index; no boxes, masks, LLM or reference image (WordNet ontology and CoreNLP parser used only to choose word pairs for the studies)
model: SD2.0 base, 512x512, 30 steps, DPM solver, guidance 7.5 (no other model tested)
similar_subjects: both objects present in 52% of cohyponym-pair images vs 61% of non-cohyponym (1,000 prompts, exact test 99%); map mIoU 46.7 vs 22.9 (0-100); within cohyponyms 71.7% correct at low overlap vs 9.75% at high; failure scored is omission, not attribute borrowing; no per-pair numbers
which_pairs: same WordNet category raises map overlap (correct images 43.5 vs 5.43 mIoU) and failure; within a category, low attention overlap (IoU at most 0.4) predicts success (71.7% vs 9.75% at IoU at least 0.6); text embeddings, appearance, token position not measured
when: not measured for the cohyponym study; segmentation ablation shows the first 15 of 30 steps give about 60.3 of the full 60.7 mIoU80 and the first step alone about 46.5 (read from Figure 11; direction of 'first' not stated)
cost: no extra passes or timings printed; maps are read from the ordinary forward pass (inferred)
headline: SD2.0 base: 52% vs 61% both-objects-present for cohyponym vs non-cohyponym pairs, with DAAM map mIoU 46.7 vs 22.9; low-overlap cohyponym pairs succeed 71.7% vs 9.75% at high overlap
suggests: (inferred) use cross-attention overlap as the leading predictor but read it at CO3's early corrected steps so it precedes the outcome; DAAM's IoU recipe (threshold 0.4, bins 0.4 and 0.6) is ready to copy; its accuracy numbers score omission and do not transfer to borrowing
